extraction_warnings: This paper's primary human demographic data (age, sex, ancestry, exact patient counts by group) are relegated to supplementary Table S1A/S1C, which were not included in the provided text; most demographic fields are therefore not_reported.

Study combines multiple experimental systems (gnotobiotic mice, bacterial isolates, ex vivo human stool incubations, and longitudinal human RA patient cohort) making a single study-level value for fields like control/case status, DNA extraction kit, and sequencing platform imprecise; values extracted pertain specifically to the NYU human RA patient cohort where stated.
Country and study_name fields were not explicitly stated and required inference or were left not_reported.

Multiple sequencing platforms (MiSeq for 16S-seq, HiSeq2500 for RNA-seq, NovaSeq for shotgun metagenomics) and DNA extraction kits (MoBio Powersoil, ZymoBIOMICS, Wizard SV 96) are used across different sample types; only the NYU human RA patient specific values were extracted for sequencing_platform and dna_extraction_kit fields.
Most schema fields (zygosity, BMI, neonatal/OBGYN fields, tumor staging, HLA, smoker) are not applicable to this RA/microbiome study and were marked not_reported.

Responder status (MTX-R/MTX-NR) is a key subgroup distinction in the paper but was not mapped to disease_response_orr as a formal ORR value due to definitional mismatch (DAS28-based response vs. ORR/RECIST); details noted in field notes.

fmt_id and fmt_role were inferred from mouse gnotobiotic colonization experiments using human donor stool, which may not align with a typical human-to-human FMT clinical trial context intended by the schema.

This paper is a microbiome/immunology study on methotrexate and gut bacteria, not a clinical oncology trial; several schema fields (OS, ECOG, tumor size) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.
The 'host_species' field is ambiguous because both human patients (sample donors) and mice (experimental hosts) are central to the study; 'human' was chosen as the primary study participant species.

biomarker fields were populated using DAS28, the only quantifiable disease-response biomarker explicitly reported; other 'biomarkers' like MIC values were considered more experimental/methodological than clinical biomarkers and were placed in uncurated_metadata instead.
